Paragraph:
Translation: Sanjaya said: O descendant of Bharata, being thus addressed by Arjuna, Lord Krsna drew up the fine chariot in the midst of the armies of both parties.

Purport: In this verse Arjuna is referred to as Gudakesa. Gudaka means sleep, and one who conquers sleep is called gudakesa. Sleep also means ignorance. So Arjuna conquered both sleep and ignorance because of his friendship with Krsna... Thus a devotee of Krsna can conquer both sleep and ignorance simply by thinking of Krsna constantly... As Hrsikesa, or the director of the senses and mind of every living entity, Krsna could understand Arjuna's purpose in placing the chariot in the midst of the armies. Thus He did so, and spoke as follows.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Responding to Arjuna's request, Krishna drives the chariot directly into the vulnerable, exposed space between the two massive armies.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: The narrator emphasizes Arjuna's title as 'Gudakesa' (conqueror of sleep/ignorance), suggesting that his awareness is sharp and elevated. Krishna, the ultimate guide, facilitates this by placing Arjuna exactly where he needs to be to face reality.
Outcome/Resolution: The chariot is positioned in the 'no man's land' between the forces, perfectly setting the stage for the ultimate confrontation and Arjuna's impending psychological crisis.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.exposure: Placing oneself in the center of the conflict

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Prajna (Awakened consciousness; overcoming the 'sleep' of ignorance or Tamas)
Samadhi (Deep focus and absorption in divine consciousness)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The movement of the chariot symbolizes the soul's journey toward truth. Krishna (the Divine Guide) deliberately places Arjuna (the awakened soul) in the center of duality—between two opposing forces—so that he can observe the illusions of the material world with perfect clarity and conquered ignorance.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is akin to the preparation phase of exposure therapy. Arjuna is wide awake ('conqueror of sleep') and highly mindful. His guide/therapist figure (Krishna) is moving him safely into the space where he must directly confront his stressors, establishing the environment necessary for deep psychological work.
